text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple CUDA OOMs detected on cluster-gpu-12 while headroom reported as available. Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.

alex: seeing repeated OOMs from runtime-daemon on node cluster-gpu-12. Headroom metrics show ~1.2GiB free but allocator logs show failing reserve claim.

maria: tagging oncall. @alex can you paste the runtime logs/stack traces?

alex: attaching snippets: `runtime: failed reserve claim id=0x3e7 size=256Mi err=OOM` then `allocator: fragmentation detected: largest_free_span=128Mi total_free=1.1GiB` so free memory exists but not contiguous.

priya: this looks like classic slab fragmentation — KV cache + model KV cache pinned a bunch of small blocks. Any recent rollout to change reserve size?

alex: no rollout in last 2hrs. But we had a batch of long-context requests ramp up to 16k tokens around same time. Could have caused heavy KV usage + prefix cache.

dan: nvidia-smi top output: `GPU-0 Memory-Used=11.4GiB Memory-Total=24GiB` but `cudaFree` calls failing. Paging events spike in dmesg: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: BAR1: BAR1 mmap failed` and some `nvlink` errors.

ops-lead: severity? Customer impact?

cs-oncall: some hosted requests returned 500s for large-model generation (~2% of traffic) and a couple of customers on Dedicated saw task failures. No broad customer outage yet but customer-reported errors increasing.

maria: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) cordon + drain the node (move lower priority jobs), 2) trigger runtime process restart on affected pods (fast), 3) reduce default reserve chunk size on cluster temporarily to allow more granularity, 4) evict KV cache prefixes for long-context models.

alex: doing step 2 now: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/runtime-daemon --field-selector spec.nodeName=cluster-gpu-12`

incident-bot: deploy-bot reported: restart started.

priya: while restart helps, I worry about ephemeral paging thrash. We should also lower the allocator's large-block threshold: set `ALLOC_LARGE_THRESHOLD=256Mi -> 64Mi` for the node. That allows the allocator to satisfy large requests with smaller spans.

dan: making the change via runtime config override on node: `redwoodctl node-config set cluster-gpu-12 allocator.large_threshold=64Mi`

alex: restart complete. Runtime logs show fewer immediate OOMs but still sporadic `reserve-claim` retries.

maria: start an automated cache eviction for the top 5 longest KV prefixes tied to the 16k token models: `runtimectl kv evict --prefix model-16k --limit 5`

ops-lead: are we seeing paging activity on host? iostat shows increased writeback from host-side swap. If we have container-level allocation then host might be thrashing.

alex: host vmstat shows high page reclaim: `pgpgin/pout ~ 5x baseline` and `oom_killer` not triggered. So kernel is swapping GPU-driver related pages — suspicious.

priya: could be reserved blocks leaking due to earlier failed allocations. Check `/sys/kernel/mm/hugepages` for anomalies and runtime reserve accounting.

alex: reserve accounting dump (trimmed): `reserved_blocks=124 used=118 free_reserves=6 pending_eviction=12` — pending_eviction is non-zero.

maria: that pending_eviction suggests we have a backlog of pinned blocks waiting to be reclaimed but allocator can't coalesce them. Two immediate mitigations: force eviction of pending reserves and reduce per-request reserve claim size (for new requests).

cs-oncall: notifying affected customers with a heads-up: currently limited impact, we are mitigating. Will post updates every 30m.

ops-lead: runbook step: if node continues to flap do an immediate migrate of Dedicated workloads off node and mark hardware for deeper investigation.

dan: executed eviction and applied `allocator.force_eviction=true` flag. Systems report some reclaimed blocks.

alex: after eviction, metrics show contiguous largest_free_span increased from 128Mi -> 512Mi. Subsequent reserve claims started succeeding. OOM rate dropped to near-zero.

maria: good. Now we need to root-cause: 1) why pending_eviction backlog happened, 2) why kernel paging spiked, 3) why BAR1 errors showed up in dmesg. Hypotheses: heavy long-context KV cache growth + a kernel-level driver regression in the latest CUDA driver we rolled last week.

priya: driver version on node: `nvidia-driver 530.41` rolled last Tue. Can we bisect by comparing nodes on older driver?

alex: yes, cluster-gpu-09 still on 525.x and hasn't shown OOMs under similar load.

dan: copying logs to incident S3: `s3://incidents/2211112223/` and creating a runbook task list.

ops-lead: next steps: - schedule postmortem, include runtime, infra, driver, and customer-impact sections - consider an emergency rollback of driver on affected nodes if we see recurrence - add automated detection for pending_eviction > 5 to trigger preemptive eviction and cordon.

maria: action items assigned: alex will collect full allocator dump + dmesg, priya will test a rollback on a single node in staging, dan will draft customer post.

cs-oncall: sent update to customers: "We're mitigating a GPU memory fragmentation issue that caused a small percentage of large-model requests to error. We've applied cache eviction and allocator tuning which resolved the immediate failures. We'll follow up with root-cause and mitigation plan."

alex: marking node as `unschedulable` for new Dedicated placement until we complete driver verification.

incident-bot: Severity set to P2. Incident channel created: #incident-2211112223.

priya: quick note for long-term: we should add finer-grained reserve slab sizes and add background coalescing in allocator to avoid fragmentation from many small KV allocations. Also consider bounded KV prefix retention when memory pressure detected.

maria: agreed. Also add a metric for `largest_free_span_bytes` and alert if it falls below 2x typical request max.

ops-lead: thanks team. Keep updates short. Next update in 15min. :thumbsup:
